business_scope.primary_industry_name: Handmade Sharp-Edge Epoxy Resin Liquid Core RPG Dice Casting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 98–127 (Limited Company) and Articles 128–356 (Company Limited by Shares); Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 4–10; Regulations on Registration of Companies (公司登記辦法)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration Section; local Municipal Company and Commerce Registration Office at the registered address
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) and Company Registration Application Form (公司登記申請書) together with the Capital Verification Report (資本查核報告書)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an ordinary limited company; the founding capital must be adequate for the intended business, deposited in a designated bank escrow account pending verification, with the capital verification report issued by a certified public accountant prior to filing
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (i) The authorized share capital of NT$1,000,000 divided into 100,000 shares at NT$10 each is ratified, and the sole founder subscribes all such shares, paid into the designated capital escrow account; (ii) the registered office located at No. 123, Section 2, Zhongxiao E. Rd., Taipei, is adopted, with authority to execute the office lease; (iii) the following officers are appointed: [Director A] as Chairman, [Director B] as General Manager, and [Director C] as Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting with full signatory powers. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce (online name reservation) and Investment Commission, MOEA (for foreign investment screening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application for the proposed English and Chinese company name and business scope, obtaining name protection for one month. In parallel, file a Foreign Investment Application with the Investment Commission, attaching shareholder identification, business plan, capital structure, and remittance schedule. The Investment Commission will issue an investment approval letter which authorizes capital remittance.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused, select alternative names and resubmit; if the Investment Commission issues a notice of deficiency, respond with additional material within 15 days or request a one-time extension of another 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign exchange bank (authorized by Central Bank of China) and certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the investment approval, remit the registered capital from the foreign shareholder's bank account to the Company's newly opened Taiwan capital escrow account. Present the investment approval letter and remittance receipt to the bank for conversion to New Taiwan Dollars; instruct the CPA to issue a Capital Verification Report after confirming receipt of the funds in the capital-special bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide supporting proof of lawful source and AML declarations; if the currency conversion is delayed, amend the remittance reference and re-present the original remittance certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce (one-stop company registration portal) or local Commerce Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the company registration application with the MOEA online portal, submitting the Articles of Incorporation, Capital Verification Report, sole shareholder's subscription form, director appointment consent, registered office lease or consent certificate, and the company registration application form. Pay the registration fee and certificate fee after the application is approved.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease agreement or certificate of consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried, rectify any deficiencies within 30 days of notice; extend the submission deadline once by 30 days with a formal letter; appeal to the MOEA administrative review board if the rejection is unsupported.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Uniform Invoice Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (local tax office) and Municipality Revenue Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the company registration certificate is obtained, register with the local tax office to obtain the tax exemption number (統一編號) and apply for the Business Tax (營業稅) registration. File for the issuance of Uniform Invoices (統一發票) after a physical inventory of the registered office and the responsible person's identity check. Engage an accountant to set up accounting books and the VAT filing cycle.
required_dossiers: Responsible person's ID and class seal
Articles of Incorporation and company seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues an inquiry regarding the business premises, provide an additional site photo and explanation; if the Uniform Invoice quota is insufficient, submit a supplementary application to the local revenue service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factory Registration and Environmental Pollution Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Bureau (IDB), MOEA; Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan; local Municipal Environmental Protection Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for Factory Registration under the Factory Management Act, submitting the factory floor plan, building right proof, equipment list, and production process details. Concurrently file an Environmental Pollution Self-Management Declaration with the EPA for the low-impact manufacturing process covering epoxy resin handling and waste disposal. If production capacity remains below the Level II threshold of the EIA Act, no full Environmental Impact Assessment is required.
required_dossiers: Factory floor plan and structural safety certificate
Manufacturing process and material safety data sheets (MSDS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IDB queries the factory layout, amend the floor plan and resubmit; if the EPA classified the operation as requiring a higher EIA tier, commence a limited environmental impact report or obtain a category registration certificate before production begins.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Safety, Fire Safety, and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Fire Department (Civil Defense Directorate), Ministry of Labor (Occupational Safety and Health Administration), and Municipal Labor Inspection Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain fire safety clearance by submitting the building's fire prevention design and evacuation plan for inspection, including adequate fire extinguishers, one safety exit per production floor, and fire alarm system. Register the workplace under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including workplace clean-up, sharp-edge tool protection, and employee injury insurance. Acquire the Civil Defense Certificate (全民防衛動員) as required for the facility's structural load and hazard classification.
required_dossiers: Fire alarm and extinguisher installation records
Workplace hazard assessment and risk registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire safety certificate is delayed, undertake corrective actions listed in the notice and schedule a pre-inspection within 10 working days; for workplace safety violations, implement a remedial action plan and obtain a conditional operation clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Bureau (IDB), Ministry of Economic Affairs; local Municipal Industrial Administration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate (工廠登記證) and Manufacturing Operation Permit (工廠營運許可證)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV – Registration/Declaration (small-scale, low-pollution production). No full EIA requirement unless the production scale exceeds 10 tonnes per month of resin material or in a designated sensitive zone; otherwise, a self-management declaration is sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Taiwan Water Pollution Control Act effluent limits (pH 6–9, chemical oxygen demand below 100 mg/L, suspended solids below 30 mg/L). Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from epoxy resin curing must be captured through a local fume hood and carbon adsorption system, with total VOC emissions not exceeding the automatic permit threshold of 0.6 kg/hour; if exceeded, an air pollution control permit is required. Waste epoxy resin, sharp-edge flashing, and liquid core residue must be classified as general industrial waste or hazardous waste (if containing reactive hardeners) and removed by a licensed contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the local Fire Department; structural load inspection certificate from a licensed structural engineer covering storage racks and casting stations; occupational safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including the installation of hand and eye protection equipment, proper storage of sharp-edged dice, and employee labor insurance registration; a Civil Defense Clearance is required for the facility’s construction type and emergency evacuation plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, R.O.C. (Taiwan) — 財政部; administered through local National Taxation Bureaus and the online e-tax portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a wholly foreign-owned Taiwan subsidiary: (1) file company incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) One-Stop Business Registration; (2) the MOEA forwards the registration to the local National Taxation Bureau; (3) the Bureau automatically assigns a Taiwan Unified Business Number (統一編號/tax ID); (4) the WFOE completes business tax registration and enrolls in the MOF E-Invoice Platform; (5) a foreign parent making direct cross-border e-commerce sales to Taiwan individuals must separately apply for cross-border e-commerce tax registration at the tax portal once annual Taiwan-source sales exceed NT$480,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available under Taiwan tax law; a Taiwan WFOE is mandatorily taxed at entity level. The only relevant elective mechanisms are the small-scale business operator deemed-tax regime (for very low turnover) and the simplified reverse-charge/self-assessment election for non-resident cross-border e-commerce suppliers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Business Tax under the Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident businesses: mandatory tax registration with no turnover exemption before commencing business. Non-resident cross-border e-commerce suppliers of electronic services: NT$480,000 annual sales threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates Uniform Invoices. Electronic invoices must be transmitted to the MOF E-Invoice Platform (電子發票整合服務平台) within the prescribed timeframe, generally by the bi-monthly VAT filing deadline; no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping is required. API-based electronic invoicing through certified service providers is mandatory for high-volume WFOE operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) goods actually exported from Taiwan, evidenced by customs export declarations and shipping documents, and (ii) services performed in Taiwan for overseas customers that are used outside Taiwan, with evidence of foreign-currency receipt or equivalent substantiation. The WFOE must maintain complete export order records, customs clearance evidence, shipping documents, and foreign-currency receipt evidence to claim the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau conducts document-by-document review of zero-rating claims. Failure to substantiate the export within the statutory time frame results in retroactive assessment of the standard 5% business tax, plus interest and a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax under Business Tax Act Article 51. Fraudulent claims may attract criminal tax evasion charges, and improperly received refunds are clawed back for the full statutory assessment period of five years, extending to seven years for willful evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with delegated foreign-exchange administration and cross-border payment monitoring performed by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a partial-convertibility framework. Current-account items such as export receipts, ordinary trade settlement, transportation, royalties, and after-tax profit or dividend remittances are generally convertible after documentary genuineness review and reporting. Capital-account items, including FDI equity injections, shareholder loans, liquidation proceeds, and cross-border guarantees, remain subject to SAFE registration, designated capital/foreign-debt account controls, and applicable quotas or approval conditions. Profit remittance hurdles for the WFOE include audited annual financial statements, corporate income tax settlement clearance, board resolution declaring the dividend, verification that registered capital has been duly contributed, and confirmation that all SAFE reporting and foreign-currency account reconciliation are current. The RMB is convertible for bona fide trade and investment-backed operating needs, but not for speculative or unauthorized cross-border capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE goods-trade administration, export proceeds must be repatriated into the WFOE's domestic foreign-currency current-account or an SAFE-approved offshore account. The statutory matching timeline follows the earlier of the contractual settlement maturity or the customs export declaration period, generally not exceeding 90 days after exportation, with advance export receipts requiring actual export within 90 days unless an extension is filed and approved. There is no mandatory fixed-percentage conversion of export receipts into CNY; exporters may retain foreign currency in approved deposit balances. However, every collection must be reconciled to an electronic customs declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, and transport document via SAFE's Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. Unreconciled or overdue export receipts can trigger enterprise status downgrading from Class A to Class B/C and result in blocked settlements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI USD/CNY paid-in capital); Operational RMB/FCY Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational RMB/FX Current Account; Export Proceeds Collection Account; Trade Settlement Facility
Operational Current Account; FX Hedging and Trade Finance Account
Capital Contribution Escrow Account; Operational Account with Documentary Trade Handling
Commercial LC Import Settlement Account; Operational Account
Operational RMB Account; Payroll, Tax, and Social Premium Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an ancillary settlement channel, but Low as a primary legal-grade banking venue. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, or neobanks generally cannot hold RMB demand deposits or issue local Chinese account numbers to the WFOE without a PRC payment institution license. They can, however, be used through licensed payment partners for inbound collection of small-value crowdfunding proceeds from Kickstarter, Stripe, or PayPal, and for outbound payments to non-Chinese suppliers, provided the underlying flows are fully reported to SAFE. The compliant route is to maintain the WFOE's primary corporate bank account at a domestic bank and connect the EMI or cross-border payment aggregator as an ancillary collection/disbursement channel, never as a substitute for the onshore treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical attendance is High for the FDI capital account and SAFE-linked FX account opening. The legal representative, or a board-designated senior officer holding a properly notarized power of attorney, must generally attend an in-person KYC interview at the chosen bank branch for the original account-opening package, including corporate chops, board resolutions, articles of association, and investor due-diligence files. Remote or video-based account opening is available only in certain pilots and only for simple domestic operational RMB accounts, not for the capital-account or cross-border settlement accounts required in this treasury blueprint. Taiwan-resident directors may appear in person at the mainland branch or delegate a local authorized representative; banks will also require valid travel documents, passport, Taiwan residence proof, and the underlying cross-strait investment registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is a Taiwan-resident shareholder whose identity, source of wealth, and shareholding trail are not immediately visible in the mainland public registries, creating a source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership underwriting red flag during the FDI account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Taiwan parent's incorporation certificate and articles of association; current register of members and UBO declaration under Chinese AML rules; audited financial statements of the parent; SAFE FDI registration and Foreign Investment Filing Certificate; board resolution approving the capital schedule and signatories; passport, Taiwan resident certificate, and proof of residence; three-year source-of-wealth evidence such as bank statements, sale agreements, tax returns, and investment account records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments arrive from online aggregators and crowdfunding platforms, specifically Kickstarter through Stripe or PayPal, rather than from named trade counterparties, which can trigger high-risk e-commerce or collect-first-ship-later AML typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform merchant due-diligence reports; transaction-level settlement statements from Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal; order-to-payment mapping; refund and chargeback history; published refund policy; product listing URLs and campaign description; customs export declarations; waybills and freight invoices; and a written operating narrative explaining the pre-sale crowdfunding manufacturing model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product descriptors containing 'dice', 'roleplay', and 'tabletop gaming' may be misclassified by screening algorithms as gambling, casino gaming, or unregulated gaming paraphernalia despite the legitimate tabletop RPG application.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product catalogue and photography; official trademarks or copyright registrations; marketing materials demonstrating non-casino tabletop roleplay use; a sworn business-model statement confirming no gambling, prize-payout, or lottery functionality; supply contracts containing end-use prohibition clauses; customer due-diligence evidence; and prior customs export declarations showing HS/ISIC product categorization under toy/game accessories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inbound and outbound settlement flows in multiple currencies, including USD, EUR, TWD, and CNY, with aggregated or partially deferred export collection schedules, may trigger a trade-authenticity and foreign-exchange mismatch review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master sales contracts and individual purchase orders; commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations, and bills of lading; supplier-side vendor contracts and inventory records; bank statements showing the cash-to-trade cycle; quarterly reconciliation between export declarations, receipts, and disbursements; and FX hedging confirmations demonstrating real underlying exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lawful manufacture of epoxy resin dice can create chemical or dangerous-goods flags when the material safety data sheet, REACH/RoHS/CE certificate, or shipping classification is absent from the corporate KYC file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Material safety data sheets (MSDS/SDS) for epoxy resins, pigments, and accelerators; REACH/RoHS/CE certificates of conformity; non-hazardous statement or UN-certified dangerous-goods packaging evidence if applicable; supplier compliance declarations and purchase invoices; product physical testing reports; finished-product photographs; and goods-in-transit plus product-liability insurance certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must be layered through SAFE's FDI framework. Step 1: complete the FDI foreign-exchange registration for the WFOE at the designated domestic bank and obtain the FDI verification reference. Step 2: open a Capital Contribution Foreign-Currency or RMB Special Capital Account exclusively for the WFOE; no equity funds may be paid into an ordinary operating account without the capital-account code. Step 3: instruct the Taiwan investor to send a standard SWIFT MT103 from a licensed Taiwan bank, with beneficiary 'CN_WFOE_LTD', beneficiary bank equal to the WFOE's onshore branch, a purpose string such as 'FDI paid-in capital - equity injection under the Articles of Association', and the remitter reference containing the SAFE FDI registration number and the WFOE's unified social credit code. Step 4: upon receipt, the onshore bank verifies the SAFE registration, account title, purpose string, amount, and beneficiary identity; converts or retains FX as instructed; records the transaction in the cross-border BOP direct-reporting system; and releases funds only after the full compliance file is verified. Verification documents include the Foreign Investment Filing Certificate, board resolution approving the capital schedule, articles of association, passport or registration certificate of the investor, bank reference letters, and audited parent financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed from the WFOE's current account through three primary clearing rails. First, SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COVER for high-value direct remittances to overseas raw-material suppliers, with the SWIFT purpose field referencing the underlying import contract and the beneficiary identical to the payee on the invoice and transport documents. Second, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit opened by the WFOE's PRC bank in favor of foreign suppliers, governed by UCP600, with settlement against presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin. Third, CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) RMB direct settlement where the supplier accepts CNY, which removes SWIFT intermediation and accelerates same-day settlement. All outbound disbursements are reported to SAFE through the BOP direct-reporting system and matched with import trade declarations, customs records, and FX purchase/sale contracts before the bank releases funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY FX forwards against USD, EUR, JPY, and HKD, supported by verified real trade receivables or payables
FX swaps between CNY and convertible foreign currencies for covering trade-working-capital maturity mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) for long-term foreign-currency funding related to the WFOE's capital structure or asset investment
Plain vanilla FX options on a current-account or investment-background underlying, requiring SAFE-qualified derivatives documentation and bank approval records

Offshore non-deliverable CNY forwards (NDFs) executed through the Taiwan parent or an offshore treasury center solely as a hedge against the consolidated USD/TWD exposure, with no onshore delivery of CNY to non-resident accounts absent SAFE approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (shareholder-approved) filed to corporate registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commercial Administration Section (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end; calendar-year filers by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NT$10,000–NT$50,000 fine; continued noncompliance triggers additional fines, compulsory completion orders, and potential court enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and annual financial report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (MOF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing period 1 May to 31 May following the fiscal year end; extensions available only after provisional payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 3% per month on underpaid tax, capped at 30%, plus daily interest; willful nonfiling triggers forced assessment, seizure, and collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Meeting resolution and statutory register updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Office (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder meeting held within first 6 months of fiscal year; registration-triggering changes filed within 15 days of resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed company registration subject to NT$10,000–NT$50,000 fine per violation; unregistered changes unopposable to third parties until properly filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit for public companies and non-public companies with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million or specifically designated by the Ministry of Economic Affairs; other non-public companies may prepare qualified financial statements without external audit unless requested by MOEA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public entities: IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public entities: Enterprise Accounting System (EAS) / Taiwan GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a standalone annual UBO return. The company must confirm ultimate beneficial ownership at each annual shareholder meeting and file any change in 10%+ beneficial ownership with MOEA within 15 days; the annual statutory declaration must affirm no unreported UBO changes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified R&D expenditures and approved smart-machinery or automation-robot investments are creditable under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; the R&D credit generally equals up to 20% of qualifying annual outlays and is directly offset against corporate income tax. A 5% retained-earnings surtax applies under Books and Records of the Income Tax Act, meaning that total corporate-level tax costs for undistributed profits may exceed the 20% headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 15) - filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing and Payment Service (財政部電子申報繳稅服務網, e-tax.etax.nat.gov.tw)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement; a provisional prepayment obligation exists for the current fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing must occur within five months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is May 31 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross business revenue, operating revenue, and non-operating income recognized under Taiwanese EAS/IFRS for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity with a Taiwan permanent establishment (PE) includes only Taiwan-source income attributable to the PE; foreign-source income is excluded unless the entity is tax-resident or otherwise subject to Taiwan CFC rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after deducting all allowable costs, expenses, losses, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident enterprise, the PE profit must be computed according to Taiwanese transfer-pricing and PE attribution rules, reflecting functions, assets, and risks of the Taiwan operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 20% on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where books and records are inadequate, the tax authority may deem the PE profit using a prescribed profit margin on gross turnover; the 20% rate remains applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions, including sales, purchases, royalties, interest, service fees, and loans, with the nature and amounts of each category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify all cross-border related-party transactions with foreign affiliates and state the ultimate parent entity; transfer-pricing documentation must be attached if aggregate related-party transaction amounts meet the statutory threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset current-year taxable income with allowable prior-year losses carryforward under Article 39.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan PE may utilize carryforward losses allocated to the PE if the enterprise filed returns on a timely basis, maintained proper accounting records, and the losses originated from the Taiwan PE's taxable profit computation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers a surcharge of up to 10% of the tax payable plus daily interest on the overdue amount; understatement or omission leading to tax underpayment may be penalized up to 2.5 times the underpaid tax; continued non-filing may result in automatic tax assessment and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A foreign corporate shareholder seeking a reduced Taiwanese dividend withholding rate under an income tax treaty must (i) obtain an Annual Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence jurisdiction, (ii) present the TRC to the Taiwan payor or the branch withholding agent prior to the dividend payment date, and (iii) file the designated non-resident withholding return and beneficial-ownership declaration with the National Taxation Bureau. The Taiwanese payer may apply the treaty rate at source only after the TRC is received; otherwise, the statutory 21% is withheld and a refund may be claimed via a subsequent administrative petition. For a PRC parent, no formal cross-strait income-tax agreement is currently in force, so the 21% final withholding rate generally applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates for royalties and interest paid to non-residents are both 20%; treaty-reduced rates under Taiwan's comprehensive DTA network commonly bring royalties to 10% and interest to 10% (or, in special circumstances, 5% for certain financial obligations). In the absence of an applicable treaty, the statutory 20% final withholding is levied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies a robust economic-substance principle through Article 12-1 of the Taxpayer Rights Protection Act and the general anti-avoidance rules in Articles 43-3 and 43-4 of the Income Tax Act. A Taiwanese WFOE will be recognized as the true profit earner only where it has business premises, employees, actual decision-making authority, and assumes meaningful operational risks. Pure paper entities without substantive activity may be disregarded, and their income reattributed to the actual principal, exposing the enterprise to reassessment and severe penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Taiwan-source sales derived from Kickstarter or PayPal transactions, issuing false VAT invoices, or inflating declared costs through fictitious suppliers or fabricated logs for manually crafted dice toys.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, a false return attracts an additional tax penalty of up to 2.5 times the underpaid tax; daily interest accrues from the original due date; criminal tax-fraud prosecution under the Tax Evasion and Tax Investigation Act may result in prison of up to five years and fines up to NT$6 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Through veil-piercing principles, directors can be ordered to make restitution of the underpaid tax plus interest; tax authorities may apply travel bans and exit controls under the Tax Collection Act; responsible officers exposing to imprisonment and personal asset seizure when the evasion is habitual or organized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Taiwan WFOE as a shell that has no employees, leased premises, product-development records, or board minutes, while profit is routed to an offshore principal through inflated management fees or aggressive dividend payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority can disregard the legal entity and reallocate the taxable income directly to the beneficial owner, levying 20% corporate income tax, 21% dividend WHT, and an understatement penalty under Article 110, together with interest; sham arrangements are also subject to a civil fine of NT$15,000 to NT$300,000 under the Taxpayer Rights Protection Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain or sign incomplete substance records may be jointly liable for the reassessed tax deficiency; personal assets may be attached if the sham structure caused irretrievable tax loss, and the director may be barred from leaving Taiwan until the deficiency is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating prices on cross-border transactions with related parties - for example undercharging sales to a foreign distributor or overpaying for resin moulds from a Hong Kong affiliate - thereby shifting profit outside Taiwan and defeating the arm's length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Taiwan's Transfer Pricing Rules and Article 43-2 of the Income Tax Act, the tax authority may make an upward adjustment to Taiwan taxable income, levy the resultant 20% corporate income tax with a shortfall penalty up to 2.5 times the deficiency, and impose civil interest from the tax's original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer-pricing documents or direct transactions without legitimate commercial rationale may be held personally accountable for the adjusted deficiency if the corporate form is found fraudulent, and could face criminal liability for document forgery under the Criminal Code, carrying imprisonment of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe, PayPal, or other payment rails to receive Kickstarter pledge funds from sanctioned persons or shell crowdfunding accounts, or failing to run beneficial-ownership due diligence on a strategic distributor who resells tabletop dice to embargoed jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act and the Weapons of Mass Destruction Anti-Proliferation Act subject the enterprise to criminal fines of up to NT$100 million and imprisonment of up to seven years; the tax authority may also deny expense deductions for unlawful payments and impose a 10% disgorgement surcharge on the affected income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who execute or authorize such transactions risk criminal prosecution, personal forfeiture orders, entry bans, and, in cross-border cases, issuance of international arrest warrants through mutual legal-assistance channels.
